transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-09 16:00 PDT
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Nina Lopez (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (Redwood CSM), Marcus Lee (Cobalt Skies CTO), Dana Ortiz (Head of ML), Evan Kim (Platform Eng), Lana Chu (Security)

Auto-summary: kickoff, intake, and pilot planning. Links shared: https://redwood.in/secure/runbooks/csk-vpc , pricing deck (internal).

00:00 Samir: hey everyone thanks for joining, i'm samir with redwood inference, excited to kick this off. quick round of intros?
00:12 Marcus: yeah i'm marcus, cto, i'll be driving infra and platform decisions, dana is on ML side, evan handles networking, lana on security.
00:25 Nina: nina lopez, solutions eng, i'll own the perf/benchmark side and help with the runtime configs.
:34 Dana: great thanks, we had a few pre-reads, but main ask is latency stable under 95th perc, and cost predictability, we run many short prompts.
01:10 Samir: totally, that tracks. quick agenda: network intake, pilot scope, dedicated vs hosted tradeoffs, security questions, and next steps.
02:02 Evan: on network - do you support VPC peering or are we using a private link? we need egress ips for firewall allowlist.
02:25 Nina: yes both options; for dedicated we recommend VPC peering for lower latency, and we can provide egress ip ranges for allowlisting. i'll follow up with the IPs. (note: sometimes transcript shows "egg rest" instead of e g r e s s)
03:01 Lana: we need SOC2 artifacts and details on KMS/HSM integrations. do you store any customer data? how is kv cache handled for private deployments?
03:40 Samir: good q - we don't persist customer prompts in hosted by default, for dedicated/private we can disable retention and integrate with your KMS. we'll send the SOC2 pack, and on the kv cache - it's local to the runtime and can be wiped and not logged. (samir says "K V cash" once)
04:12 Marcus: can you summarize the dedicated SLA and what we can expect for p99 latency?
04:30 Samir: dedicated gives predictable throughput; typical p95 numbers depend on model/seq length. nina: maybe you can throw some ballpark numbers?
04:46 Nina: for a 8k context medium-sized model on A100-equivalent, 95th is around 150-220 ms for short prompts, quantized variants hit higher throughput but may add 10-30ms. we'll capture exact numbers in the benchmark. (note: i said "A one hundred" which sometimes the transcript shows as "A one hundred")
06:12 Dana: we're sensitive to hallucination on long summaries, so we'll want to run evals during the pilot and have rollback if quality regresses.
06:40 Nina: absolutely - we'll include eval prompt set and quality thresholds; Redwood Optimize recommendations can help with batching and quantization, though sometimes docs show it as "Red wood Optimize".
08:05 Marcus: timeline — we'd like pilot in two weeks, production in ~8 weeks after pilot if all goes well. is that feasible?
08:25 Samir: yes pilot in ~2 weeks is doable. pilot scope idea: 1) deploy dedicated pool for 2 weeks, 2) run perf + quality evals, 3) verify SLOs and security controls.
09:10 Evan: what infra do you need from our side? VPC peering, egress allowlist, any certs for mTLS?
09:40 Nina: VPC peering + route tables, allowlist, and we'd like to test mTLS for control plane if you require it. we'll send a checklist. link to runbook: https://redwood.in/secure/runbooks/csk-vpc
11:05 Lana: encryption — at rest and in transit? also key management. we prefer customer-managed keys (CMK) in KMS.
11:30 Samir: we support customer-managed KMS for private/dedicated; for hosted we can offer envelope encryption and integrate to your KMS per contract. we'll attach the KMS integration doc.
13:00 Dana: on model variants — we want to test a mid-size open model and a quantized fast variant. does your runtime support continuous batching and prefix caching?
13:28 Nina: yes, runtime supports continuous batching, kv caching, and automatic prefix cache; sometimes transcript shows "prefix cash". we'll configure batching policy to keep latency under SLO.
15:15 Marcus: cost — we need an estimate for running 100k requests/month with average length 60 tokens. what's the delta between hosted and dedicated?
15:40 Samir: hosted is usage-based, dedicated is committed capacity so better unit economics at scale. i'll share a simple cost pro-forma. also mention of "Optimize" cost tooling that suggests batch sizes and quantization.
17:02 Evan: network egress to cloud — do you need static NAT?
17:20 Nina: we can provide static egress ips for allowlisting. for private on-prem we have an air-gapped packaging option but that requires more lead time.
18:45 Marcus: legal/contract — we'll need standard indemnity and data residency clauses. who on your side handles enterprise contracts?
19:00 Samir: our sales ops legal team handles that; i'll include the contact and the contract template with the pricing email.
20:15 Lana: audit logs — we need detailed audit trails for requests, who accessed model configs, and change history.
20:40 Priya: console has per-route auditing and token-level logs; we can enable retention to meet your compliance needs. we'll share sample audit export.
22:05 Dana: one technical nit — we have bursts around 10am UTC, how do autoscaling and burst caps work on dedicated? can it handle sudden spikes?
22:28 Nina: dedicated has configurable autoscaling and a burst pool you can enable; we can set policies to preserve latency SLOs while capping cost. we can also route lower-priority traffic to a cheaper variant during spikes.
24:10 Marcus: any known blockers for getting pilot started quickly?
24:25 Samir: biggest blockers are network allowlisting and signed MSA if you want enterprise terms. tech-wise we can spin a dedicated pool quickly once we have the VPC peering and egress rules.
26:00 Evan: i'll need the exact peering CIDR and guidance - can you provide a template?
26:18 Nina: yes template will be in the runbook link, i'll send a direct copy in the follow-up.
28:00 Priya: proposed pilot success criteria — p95 latency < 250ms for 95% of requests, quality eval pass rate > 92% on seed tests, and no security gaps flagged in initial review. agree?
28:30 Marcus: sounds good, maybe add cost per 1k tokens under $X as a target.
29:05 Samir: noted — we'll include cost target in the pro-forma.
31:20 Dana: will Redwood provide a small trial dataset for QA or do we need to forward ours?
31:40 Nina: you can upload your test prompts; we can also seed with synthetic tests but recommend your real prompts for quality checks.
33:10 Evan: any special network ports?
33:30 Nina: standard https 443, maybe 80 for healthchecks; we'll detail in checklist.
35:00 Lana: need to confirm data residency — is any processing done outside region?
35:25 Samir: for dedicated you can pin region; for hosted we have regional endpoints, we can ensure processing in chosen region per contract.
37:00 Marcus: ok recap?
37:10 Priya: recap - Samir to send pricing and contract template; Nina to publish benchmark plan and runbook; Evan to share network diagrams; Lana to enumerate compliance controls; Priya will schedule weekly 30-min pilot sync.
38:05 Samir: i'll also include link to bench spreadsheet and suggested VM types and quantization knobs.
40:00 Dana: timeline check — we'll aim to have network and legal cleared in week one so pilot can start week two.
41:30 Evan: noted, i'll prioritize the diagram and firewall rules.
44:00 Nina: one more technical note — if you plan to use KV cache across sessions we need to discuss TTLs, otherwise we recommend per-request cache for PII workloads.
44:40 Marcus: that's helpful, we'll default to per-request and adjust after pilot.
46:10 Priya: next meeting — propose 2026-04-13 for security deep-dive to review SOC2 artifacts and KMS mapping.
46:35 Lana: works for me.
47:00 Samir: perfect, i'll send invites and follow-ups after this call.
49:20 Marcus: thanks everyone.
49:35 Meeting end

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hearings (e.g., "Red wood" vs Redwood, "K V cash" vs KV cache, "A one hundred" vs A100), filler words, and speaker label jitter were left in to maintain authenticity.
